blocks.content: STATE LEGISLATURE

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 168 provides for the composition of State Legislatures, consisting of the Governor and one or two Houses depending on the state.
Under Article 169, Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council if the State Assembly passes a resolution supported by a special majority.
Currently, six states—Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, and Maharashtra—have a bicameral legislature.
The Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is directly elected by the people, whereas the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is a permanent, indirectly elected body.
The Legislative Assembly holds dominant power over Money Bills and executive accountability compared to the Legislative Council.

blocks.content: The State Legislature is one of the most important organs of the State Government in India. It represents the democratic will of the people at the state level and performs law-making, financial, and supervisory functions.

Just as Parliament functions at the national level, the State Legislature functions at the state level. It plays a vital role in ensuring democracy, accountability, and good governance within the State.
The provisions relating to State Legislature are mentioned in Part VI of the Indian Constitution (Articles 168–212).
NEED FOR STATE LEGISLATURE IN A FEDERAL SYSTEM
India follows a federal structure of government where powers are divided between:
Since states have their own subjects to legislate upon, a separate legislature is required at the state level.
The State Legislature:

items:
• Makes laws on State List and Concurrent List
  • Controls the State Executive
  • Represents regional aspirations
  • Strengthens democratic decentralization

LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY (VIDHAN SABHA) – DETAILED STUDY
The Legislative Assembly is the lower house and the most powerful body in the State Legislature. Composition:

items:
• Members are directly elected by the people
  • Maximum strength – 500
  • Minimum strength – 60 (can be less in smaller states)
  • Term – 5 years
  • Can be dissolved earlier by Governor
Members are directly elected by the people
Minimum strength – 60 (can be less in smaller states)
Can be dissolved earlier by Governor

blocks.content: Qualifications of Members:

items:
• Citizen of India
  • Minimum age – 25 years
  • Not holding any office of profit
Not holding any office of profit

blocks.content: The Legislative Assembly represents the will of the people and controls the government.
POWERS OF LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY
The Legislative Assembly enjoys extensive powers: LEGISLATIVE POWERS:

items:
• Makes laws on State List
  • Makes laws on Concurrent List
  • Can amend or repeal existing state laws
Can amend or repeal existing state laws

blocks.content: Article 168 prescribes the constitution of State Legislatures consisting of the Governor and the Legislative Assembly, along with the Legislative Council in bicameral states.
FINANCIAL POWERS:

items:
• Money Bill can be introduced only here
  • Budget is passed here
  • Controls state expenditure

items:

blocks.content: CONSTITUTIONAL POWERS:

items: • Participates in amendment of Constitution (in some cases)

blocks.content: LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL (VIDHAN PARISHAD) – DETAILED
The Legislative Council is the upper house of the State Legislature. Nature:

items:
• Permanent House
  • Cannot be dissolved
  • 1/3 members retire every 2 years

blocks.content: Composition:
Mode of Election:

items:
• 1/3 elected by MLAs
  • 1/3 by local authorities
  • 1/12 by teachers
  • 1/12 by graduates
  • 1/6 nominated by Governor

blocks.content: The Council acts as a revising and advisory body.
POWERS OF LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL

rows: Exclusive right to introduce and pass
Can delay up to 14 days only; no veto power
Cannot be dissolved, but can be completely abolished

items:
• Can introduce ordinary bills
  • Can delay ordinary bills for 3 months
  • Can delay Money Bills for only 14 days
  • Can suggest amendments
  • Cannot remove Council of Ministers
Can delay ordinary bills for 3 months
Can delay Money Bills for only 14 days

blocks.content: Thus, the Legislative Council has limited powers.
ROLE OF GOVERNOR IN STATE LEGISLATURE
The Governor is an integral part of the State Legislature. Powers:

items:
• Summons and prorogues legislature
  • Addresses the first session
  • Gives assent to bills
  • Can reserve bills for President
  • Can dissolve Legislative Assembly

blocks.content: The Governor acts mostly on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

blocks.content: CONTROL OVER EXECUTIVE
The State Legislature controls the Executive through:

items:
• Question Hour
  • Zero Hour
  • Calling Attention Motions
  • No-confidence Motion
  • Adjournment Motions

blocks.content: PRIVILEGES OF STATE LEGISLATURE

items:
• Freedom of speech inside House
  • Freedom from arrest in civil cases
  • Right to regulate internal proceedings
  • Right to punish for contempt
Freedom from arrest in civil cases

blocks.content: CREATION AND ABOLITION OF LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL

items: Parliament creates or abolishes a Legislative Council under Article 169, but this requires an Assembly resolution passed by a special majority.
Money Bills can only originate in the Vidhan Sabha; the Vidhan Parishad has a maximum delay period of 14 days.
Unlike the Rajya Sabha at the Centre, the Legislative Council can be completely abolished by Parliament under constitutional provisions.
Minimum age eligibility: 25 years for Vidhan Sabha members and 30 years for Vidhan Parishad members.

blocks.content: CONCLUSION
The State Legislature is the backbone of democracy at the state level.
It ensures accountability, transparency and participation of people in governance.
A strong and effective State Legislature is essential for the success of Indian federalism and democracy.
